payload.recallText: Hi, I grew up in providence rhode island, and for my whole childhood, we felt like we were part of the kennedy family. We were Irish catholics just like them, so their tragedies felt like our own. I remember crying in the back of the car during the tenth anniversary of JFK’s death, and my dad told me never to be ashamed to cry for that man. My parents even got married in the same church as Jack and Jackie. Every summer, my four aunts would take us to a beach house in Hyannis right near the Kennedy compound. But they didn't go to the beach to swim; they went to spy. They'd sit in the sun with binoculars all day, tracking everyone from Rose to Ethel and trying to figure out which kids belonged to Bobby. One year, when we were nine, me and my cousins drifted out to sea in a tiny plastic boat with no oars. We were terrified until a power boat showed up with David and Michael Kennedy! They saved us and brought us back to shore.Our aunts were ready to kill us for being so reckless, but as soon as they saw the Kennedys, they started fake smiling and acting all fancy. They were more upset that we bothered the Kennedys than they were about us almost drowning. Later that week, we were playing chicken fight in the water with my Uncle Al. I accidentally kicked him in the head, and his prosthetic eyeball popped out and sank! We didn't even know he had a fake eye. Everyone was screaming and crying until we finally found it in the sand an hour later. Looking back, I realized the Kennedy kids had been standing on the beach watching the whole crazy scene.
